Testimony

/TES-tuh-moh-nee/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Testimony means a formal statement or declaration given as evidence, especially one made under oath by a witness in court

Testimony means a formal statement given as evidence, especially one made under oath by a witness in court. The entire case turned on the testimony of a neighbor who calmly described the crash she had watched from her front porch.

Worked Example

The structural engineer's testimony about the cracked support beams convinced the jury that the builder had ignored clear warnings for years.

The engineer is delivering a formal, sworn account in court, and her statement serves as evidence in the case — that is exactly what testimony means.

How Testimony Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

deposition

deposition: a formal sworn statement recorded outside the courtroom

attestation

attestation: a formal declaration that something is true

account

account: a description of events as someone experienced them

Antonyms

retraction

retraction: the formal withdrawal of a statement one made earlier

concealment

concealment: deliberately hiding what one knows

How Strong Is It? — comment → confession → testimony

comment vs. testimony

comment vs. testimony: A comment is a casual remark anyone can toss out with no consequences, but testimony is a formal statement given under oath as evidence.

confession vs. testimony

confession vs. testimony: A confession is even weightier than testimony: instead of describing what you witnessed, you are formally admitting your own guilt.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of testimony.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — testi-

Root — testi-: witness (Latin testis)

Suffix — -mony

Suffix — -mony: forms nouns of state, condition, or action (Latin -monium)

Put it together

Put it together: Testimony is literally the 'condition of being a witness' — the statement a witness delivers. The same testis root powers testify, testament, and attest.

Use the root in a new word: attest

Use the root in a new word: attest: The notary attested that the signature on the will was genuine.

Root Check

Word Choice

Formal / legal

Testimony is what a witness says — a formal statement offered as evidence, usually under oath. Don't confuse it with a testimonial (a public tribute or product endorsement). And keep it separate from condemnation, a word taught elsewhere in this unit meaning strong public disapproval: testimony reports facts, while condemnation passes judgment.
